generated_by: tools/per-call-url-guard.mjs with three native SDK adapters. Every observation is execution output; none is hand-written.
scope: Whether a provider url passed for ONE call is refused before any request when it names a loopback, private, link-local, metadata or unspecified address, through Prism.text().using() on the openai provider and on a named openai-compatible entry. Configured urls are not checked and appear here only as controls.
encoding: An observation is whether any request was sent and which refusal code stopped the call (private_address_refused, scheme_not_allowed, non_ascii_host_use_punycode or null). The message is outside the contract and is not recorded.

cases.title: an opt-out of "1" is not true
cases.notes: Only true opts in; a truthy-looking value must not.

cases.title: per call: sharp s in a public name

A UTS46 deviation character: transitional and nontransitional IDNA convert it to different names, so the guard and the HTTP client could judge different hosts. Refused in every host, public names included.

cases.title: per call: capital sharp s inside localhost
cases.notes: Hostile: the caller chose this host for one call, and it must be refused before any request. U+1E9E maps to the deviation character sharp s under UTS46; one IDNA converter keeps it and returns punycode, another spells it "ss". Refused anywhere in the authority, like sharp s itself.

cases.title: per call: an international name in punycode

cases.notes: A non-ASCII host is refused with its own code in every language. Under IDNA conversion the reference refused this name (bidi rule) while the ports accepted it.

cases.notes: A legitimate name that needs U+200C. Each language's clean-url check refuses the joiner before the guard runs, so no refusal code is recorded; its punycode form is accepted (each language's regression rows).
